item: ADVERSARIAL CHECK of lane S1 (mcp-refresh-audit 2026-09-19) — spawn-failure triad: cloud-hub + search-hub git-crypt locked stores; tooluniverse 1.2.4 unsatisfiable fitz pin; fix = git-crypt unlock + pin bump 1.2.4 -> 1.5.0.
notes: VERDICT SAFE — no load-bearing claim broke under different instruments; zero corrections. Re-verified with DIFFERENT instruments than S1 used (this lane had NO local shell/file tools — only network fetch — so local claims got cross-session/cross-origin corroboration instead of re-execution). (1) FITZ UNSATISFIABLE — CONFIRMED via PyPI simple index https://pypi.org/simple/fitz/ (different endpoint than S1's JSON API): the ONLY file in existence is fitz-0.0.0.tar.gz; no 0.0.1.dev2, no prerelease, no other version — so 'fitz>=0.0.1.dev2' has no satisfying candidate and S1's 'no fitz prerelease exists' is exact. Hard-dep presence CONFIRMED from upstream source tag raw.githubusercontent.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/v1.2.4/pyproject.toml (different origin than built-artifact metadata): verbatim 'fitz>=0.0.1.dev2' in base deps. (2) FIX DIRECTION 1.5.0 — CONFIRMED via simple index (highest version 1.5.0, nothing above; 1.2.4 present; 1.3.x and 1.4.x lines exist so 'drift = 3 minor versions' is accurate) and via source tags: v1.5.0 pyproject.toml DROPS fitz from base deps (word appears only in a comment about the removed placeholder), pymupdf>=1.24.3 sits only under the 'pdf' extra deliberately excluded from 'all' (AGPL), mcp[cli]>=1.29.0,<2.0.0 and fastmcp>=3.4.5,<4.0.0 exactly as S1 stated — the version-bound risk note (mcp floor 1.9.3->1.29.0, fastmcp 2.12->3.4, tool surface may differ) is verbatim-correct against source. Strengthening datum: 1.2.6 exists on the same dead 1.2 line (also pre-fitx-drop), so there is no patch-level escape hatch — the bump must cross to >=1.3.0 and 1.5.0 is the right target. Bonus corroboration of S1's open question: v1.5.0's own comment says scipy 'was previously reaching installs only as a transitively of that fitz placeholder' — upstream documents that the fitz dep used to resolve in practice, supporting 'the pin died when the placeholder vanished from PyPI, not at pin time' (still UNVERIFIED as history). (3) GIT-CRYPT ROOT CAUSE (cloud-hub/search-hub) — NOT mechanically re-verified: no Bash/Read/Write instrument surfaced in this lane (three targeted tool searches returned none; only WebFetch available), so S1's byte-check/status/spawn probes could not be re-run. Corroboration instead: my own session's MCP-connect banner (surfaced in tool-search diagnostics, independent of S1's session) shows the identical six CONNECTION_CLOSED failures including cloud-hub, search-hub, tooluniverse (+ bedrock-claude, pubmed-tool, openalex-alt — S1's residual-sweep note is accurate); the 2026-07-24 'git-crypt+worktree breaks test_hub' memory S1 cited exists verbatim in my own auto-memory index (citation real, not fabricated); no contradicting evidence found. Root cause stands on S1's three independent local mechanisms (stderr traceback + od magic bytes + git-crypt status) — single-lane but multi-instrument. LIMITS / not re-verified by checker: the 157-package 1.5.0 full resolution (S1's uv pip compile alone — I had no second resolver; settling experiment unchanged: complete one 'uvx tooluniverse==1.5.0' cold build + MCP-initialize probe before calling the bump green); the literal 1.2.4 pin bytes in .agents/agents.json and .claude.json (agent-claimed extract only — no local read; sync-script step makes live follow SSOT anyway); git-crypt key location (owner-supplied, correctly gated as UNVERIFIED by S1). RECOMMENDATION: accept S1 spec unchanged; sibling lanes should test bedrock-claude / pubmed-tool / openalex-alt against the same two failure classes (git-crypt locked store; unsatisfiable uvx pin) per S1's residual sweep — my independent banner observation makes those three the highest-value next probes.
